fields.Front: Why can't PROFESSOR M:N Teaches COURSE be mapped with a 'Teaches' column in PROFESSOR listing 'CS3319, CS2210'?
fields.Back: Cells must be atomic (first normal form); a list in a cell is not a valid relation. Neither side is a 'one' side, so no single foreign key works.

fields.Front: State the rule for mapping a many-to-many relationship.
fields.Back: Make a NEW table; its key is the combination of the keys of the participating entities (both as foreign keys); also include any attributes of the relationship in the new table.

fields.Front: TEACHES table for Laura & Doug teach CS3319; Doug, Laura, Jamie teach CS2210; Doug teaches CS1027; Irving & Stuart teach MA2222: list the rows.

fields.Text: TEACHES has primary key {{c1::(EmpID, CourseNumber)}} and foreign keys {{c2::EmpID (to PROFESSOR) and CourseNumber (to COURSE)}}.

fields.Front: How is a professor who teaches nothing (Michael) represented in the M:N mapping?
fields.Back: He simply has no rows in TEACHES; no nulls are needed.

fields.Front: Map MOVIE (M) Stars (N) ACTOR with relationship attribute Salary.
fields.Back: Movie(MovieID, Title, Cost, ReleaseDate); Actor(ActorID, FirstName, LastName, BirthDate); Starring(MovieID FK, ActorID FK, Salary) with PK (MovieID, ActorID).

fields.Front: How is a ternary relationship mapped?
fields.Back: Take all the keys involved, put them in a new table as foreign keys; together they form the new primary key; include any extra attributes. E.g. rr(aid, bid, cid, rattr).

fields.Text: An M:N relationship maps to a {{c1::new table}} whose primary key is {{c2::the combination of both entities' keys}}, plus any {{c3::relationship attributes}}.

fields.Front: How does the instructor verify that (CourseNumber, EmpID) is a valid key for TEACHES?
fields.Back: No pair such as (CS3319, 11) appears twice; CourseNumber alone repeats and EmpID alone repeats, but the combination makes each row unique.

fields.Text: In TEACHES, the two key columns are also {{c1::foreign keys}} because they come from the PROFESSOR and COURSE tables.

fields.Front: What is the instructor's first (failed) attempt at representing Teaches?
fields.Back: A Teaches column in PROFESSOR holding 'CS3319, CS2210'; it is not in first normal form, so it is rejected.

fields.Front: What correction does the instructor make about the ternary-relationship slide?
fields.Back: It should read many-to-many-to-many; the rule is the same as for M:N with three keys forming the new table's key.

fields.Text: Most relationships are {{c1::binary}}; ternary relationships are {{c2::not as common}} but the mapping rule is the same.

fields.Front: What are the objectives of the M:N mapping video?
fields.Back: Represent a many-to-many relationship in a relational model, and correctly map a ternary relationship with three entities.
